source: FLEURS dev transcripts, through bournemouth_aligner's std G2P
note: The script leaves most vowels out, so the G2P supplies them: listen for them rather than trusting the spelling. Emphatic consonants (tˤ sˤ) are tokens of their own. Sindhi and Urdu aspirated and breathy stops (kʰ, bʰ, dʰ …) are single tokens; the puff after the release belongs to the stop.

SIL.name: silence
SIL.plain: A pause: no speech. Use it for a pause the speaker makes inside a segment.

noise.name: noise
noise.plain: A non-speech sound: a breath, cough, laugh or click.

<unk>.name: unknown
<unk>.plain: The G2P wrote a sound this model has no token for. Keep its time span; the label cannot say what it is.

s.name: voiceless alveolar fricative
s.plain: s. Also used for ş, which this model has no token of its own for

e.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel
e.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”

o.name: close-mid back rounded vowel
o.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”

d.name: voiced alveolar stop
d.plain: d as in “dog”. Also used for dˤ, which this model has no token of its own for

ɪ.name: near-close front unrounded vowel
examples: ɪ s t e m a l
ɪ s t e m a l
a l a t e ɪ

ɾ.name: alveolar tap
ɾ.plain: one quick flap of the tongue, as in Spanish “pero”

f.name: voiceless labiodental fricative
examples: e s t e f ɒ d e
m ʊ x t a l ɪ f

j.name: palatal approximant
examples: b a j j i n

ə.name: mid central vowel (schwa)
examples: p ə n ə h ə n ʌ ɟ i
s ə q a f ə t

b.name: voiced bilabial stop
examples: ʕ a b b a r a

ɛ.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel
examples: s y p ɛ ʁ ɡ

w.name: labial-velar approximant
examples: t u k a w w i n
ɛ n ɛ s w e

ɑ.name: open back unrounded vowel
ɑ.plain: a as in “father”. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

v.name: voiced labiodental fricative
examples: c a v a y î

ɡ.name: voiced velar stop
ɡ.plain: g as in “go”. Also used for ɢ, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: s ə ɡ ʌ h i

ʔ.name: glottal stop
ʔ.plain: the catch in the throat in “uh-oh”

ɔ.name: open-mid back rounded vowel
examples: s ɔ p ə r ɟ i

ʊ.name: near-close back rounded vowel
examples: m ʊ x t a l ɪ f

ʃ.name: voiceless postalveolar fricative
examples: ʕ a ʃ ʃ a r a

ʁ.name: voiced uvular fricative
ʁ.plain: the r of French and German
examples: s y p ɛ ʁ ɡ

x.name: voiceless velar fricative
examples: n e x o s x a n e

ð.name: voiced dental fricative
ð.plain: th as in “this”. Also used for ðˤ, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: h a ð ð a h u

q.name: voiceless uvular stop
q.plain: a k made further back, at the uvula (Uzbek “q”)
examples: t̪ ə h q i q

ʒ.name: voiced postalveolar fricative
examples: j a d ʒ u b

ʂ.name: voiceless retroflex fricative
ʂ.plain: a hard sh with the tongue tip back (Polish “sz”)

ɣ.name: voiced velar fricative
ɣ.plain: a g where the tongue does not close (Dutch g, Spanish g between vowels)
examples: ɣ a l i b a j a

y.name: close front rounded vowel
y.plain: ee said with rounded lips (French “tu”, German “über”)
examples: s y p ɛ ʁ ɡ

ħ.name: voiceless pharyngeal fricative
ħ.plain: a strong h squeezed in the throat (Arabic ح)

ɳ.name: retroflex nasal
ɳ.plain: n with the tongue tip curled back

œ.name: open-mid front rounded vowel
œ.plain: e as in “bed” said with rounded lips (French “neuf”, German “können”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

tˤ.name: voiceless alveolar stop, pharyngealised (emphatic)
tˤ.plain: t as in “ten”; pharyngealised (emphatic): said with the tongue root pulled back: a darker, “heavy” sound (Arabic ط, ص)

sˤ.name: voiceless alveolar fricative, pharyngealised (emphatic)
sˤ.plain: s; pharyngealised (emphatic): said with the tongue root pulled back: a darker, “heavy” sound (Arabic ط, ص)
examples: a l sˤ e ɪ d

ʈ.name: voiceless retroflex stop
ʈ.plain: t with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rt”)
examples: s e ʈ l a i ʈ
r ə p o r ʈ

tʰ.name: voiceless alveolar stop, aspirated
tʰ.plain: t as in “ten”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

θ.name: voiceless dental fricative
examples: t æ ʔ θ i ɾ

t̪.name: voiceless alveolar stop, dental
t̪.plain: t as in “ten”; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth
examples: t̪ a d r i d ʒ i h a

c.name: voiceless palatal stop
c.plain: a k made against the hard palate, close to “ty” (Hungarian “ty”, Czech “ť”)
examples: z o r c a r

ç.name: voiceless palatal fricative
ç.plain: the ch of German “ich”; like a strong h before ee

õ.name: close-mid back rounded vowel, nasalised
õ.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

d͡ʒ.name: voiced postalveolar affricate
examples: a l w e d͡ʒ e b a t e

kʰ.name: voiceless velar stop, aspirated
kʰ.plain: k as in “key”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ă.name: open front unrounded vowel, extra-short
ă.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; extra-short: a very short version of the vowel. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ɖ.name: voiced retroflex stop
ɖ.plain: d with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rd”)
examples: ɟ ə ɖ ə h ʌ n

ʋ.name: labiodental approximant
ʋ.plain: a soft v without friction (Dutch w, Slovenian v)

pʰ.name: voiceless bilabial stop, aspirated
pʰ.plain: p as in “pen”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɟ.name: voiced palatal stop
ɟ.plain: a g made against the hard palate, close to “dy” (Hungarian “gy”, Czech “ď”)

ẽ.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ẽ.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

ã.name: open front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ã.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

χ.name: voiceless uvular fricative
χ.plain: a rougher ch made at the uvula (Welsh “ch”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

î.name: long close front vowel (Kurdish î)
î.plain: ee as in “see”, long. The G2P writes Kurdish î as in Kurdish Latin spelling; not a pitch accent
examples: k a r î ɡ e r î

ê.name: long close-mid front vowel (Kurdish ê)
ê.plain: e as in Spanish “de”, long. Kurdish ê as in Kurdish Latin spelling; not a pitch accent
examples: h e n d ê k

í.name: close front unrounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
í.plain: ee as in “see”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

û.name: long close back vowel (Kurdish û)
û.plain: oo as in “food”, long. Kurdish û as in Kurdish Latin spelling; not a pitch accent

a͡ʊ.name: diphthong a to ʊ
a͡ʊ.plain: ow as in “now”. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

cʰ.name: voiceless palatal stop, aspirated
cʰ.plain: a k made against the hard palate, close to “ty” (Hungarian “ty”, Czech “ť”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ŋ̩.name: velar nasal, syllabic
ŋ̩.plain: ng as in “sing”; syllabic: forms a syllable with no vowel, as the n of “button”

ř.name: alveolar trill (Kurdish ڕ)
ř.plain: a strongly rolled r, the Kurdish ڕ (written ř in Kurdish Latin spelling)

ʈʰ.name: voiceless retroflex stop, aspirated
ʈʰ.plain: t with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rt”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: ɟ e s e m ʈʰ a j ã

bʰ.name: voiced bilabial stop, aspirated
bʰ.plain: b as in “bed”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

dʰ.name: voiced alveolar stop, aspirated
dʰ.plain: d as in “dog”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɡʰ.name: voiced velar stop, aspirated
ɡʰ.plain: g as in “go”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɟʰ.name: voiced palatal stop, aspirated
ɟʰ.plain: a g made against the hard palate, close to “dy” (Hungarian “gy”, Czech “ď”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɖʰ.name: voiced retroflex stop, aspirated
ɖʰ.plain: d with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rd”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: ɖʰ u n ɖ n e

ʌ̃.name: open-mid back unrounded vowel, nasalised
ʌ̃.plain: u as in “cup”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)
